title: ByteDance researchers identify cause of inconsistent long-context retrieval in DeepSeek models
key_facts: Researchers from ByteDance's Seed team identified a mechanism behind inconsistent long-context retrieval in DeepSeek models.
Chunked KV-cache compression makes retrieval accuracy depend on where information falls in a compression window.
Differences reach up to 40 percentage points across positions.
The technique compresses groups of consecutive tokens into fewer cache entries to cut memory and attention costs.
The team calls the pattern 'phase sensitivity' and reproduced it in models trained from scratch.
Different attention components specialise in retrieving from different positions.
The findings explain how strong average benchmark results can hide recurring retrieval weaknesses.
quote_evidence: Their study found that chunked KV-cache compression makes retrieval accuracy sensitive to where information falls within a compression window, producing differences of up to 40 percentage points across positions.

why_it_matters_hint: May explain why long-context AI sometimes misses facts that sit in the wrong position.
notes: Short item based on a ByteDance Seed paper; no outside review or response from DeepSeek reported.
